title: Two-round Euler liar probability bound
statement: Let $N>1$ be an odd composite natural number, and let $\ell$ be a natural number such that $8N\le 2^\ell$. Run two Euler liar tests for $N$, each using an independent block of $\ell$ uniformly random bits to form its candidate by interpreting the block as a binary integer, reducing it modulo $N-1$, and adding $1$. The probability that both rounds accept, using $2\ell$ uniformly random bits, is at most $\frac13$.
